candidates.label: Choriocarcinoma (non-seminomatous germ cell tumor) with retroperitoneal and pulmonary metastases
Mixed non-seminomatous germ cell tumor (e.g., embryonal carcinoma with choriocarcinoma) with metastases
Testicular germ cell tumor (non-seminomatous) with retroperitoneal and pulmonary metastases (occult primary)
Extragonadal germ cell tumor (primary retroperitoneal) with pulmonary metastases
Poorly differentiated carcinoma with β-hCG secretion (e.g., adrenal cortical carcinoma or other retroperitoneal malignancy) with metastases

response.rationale: The combination of elevated and rising β-hCG, a large hemorrhagic retroperitoneal mass, pulmonary nodules, and a poorly differentiated tumor with β-hCG positivity strongly favors choriocarcinoma. The differential includes other germ cell tumors and a possible testicular primary, but the classic hemorrhagic presentation and β-hCG pattern make choriocarcinoma the most likely. The absence of a testicular mass does not exclude an occult primary, but extragonadal origin is less common. Other β-hCG-secreting carcinomas are rare and less consistent with the clinical picture.
